subject: Emotions
title: Medical Professionals and Disgust
description: A micro-lesson that makes Medical Professionals and Disgust usable.

hook.text: First-year medical students often faint during cadaver dissection. By the third year, they eat lunch nearby.

buildup.text: Doctors, nurses, and paramedics must override one of the brain's strongest reflexes to do their jobs.

discovery.text: Repeated exposure desensitizes the insula. The disgust signal fades with practice, not willpower.

twist.text: Some desensitization carries over. Surgeons score lower on emotional sensitivity in personal life too.

climax.text: The tradeoff is real. Reducing disgust to treat patients can reduce empathy outside the hospital.

punchline.text: Healing others sometimes costs a piece of your own feeling.

quiz.question: What happens to the insula with repeated exposure to disgust triggers?
